exteriorDecor.comment: gate braziers at the south entrance
gargoyles watching from the keep corners
dark crystals creeping through the court
bone piles and graves in the wards
nothing alive grows here — dead trees along the walls
iron fence stubs framing the court

npcs.name: Vask
dialogue: I served this citadel once. I don't talk about that, usually.
You keep coming back here. Most people don't, once they've seen the Outer Ward.

npcs.name: The Castellan
dialogue: Welcome to Dreadspire. The master is out. The master has been out for four hundred years.
I maintain the citadel. The dust maintains itself — it's quite industrious.
The dark crystals that anchor these walls have been... wandering off lately. It is most irregular.

npcs.name: The Bound Knight
dialogue: I swore to guard this gate until my lord returns. He has not returned. I am very good at my job.
Death is a poor excuse for missing a shift here. The garrison re-forms by morning, every morning.
If you mean the citadel harm, I must stop you. If you mean it well, I must watch you suspiciously. Those are the rules.

npcs.name: Warlock Vesska
dialogue: Mind the sigils. The floor ones bite. The ceiling ones are merely judgmental.
Four centuries of research and I have proven, conclusively, that the dead make poor conversationalists.
If Ordrin asks, I did NOT borrow his shadow-oil. I liberated it. There is a difference.

work: Mind the sigils while I work. The floor ones bite, remember.
idle-chat: Even a warlock needs a moment away from the sigils. Don't tell Ordrin I said that.

npcs.name: Cultist Ordrin
dialogue: The circle is hungry. The circle is always hungry. I keep telling it we eat at dusk, like civilised people.
One bone dust, one measure of shadow-oil, one candle of rendered dread. Is that so much to ask?
Vesska took my shadow-oil. I can tell. The circle sulks differently when the oil is wrong.

npcs.name: Bone-Keeper Mald
dialogue: Every bone in its niche. Every niche labelled. Chaos is for the living.
We had a thief. Took three femurs and a favourite skull. The skull I shall miss; it was a good listener.
You want the deep ossuary? Mind the draught. And the things that enjoy the draught.

npcs.name: The Shrine-Tender
dialogue: The shadow listens, pilgrim. It is a poor talker but an excellent listener.
Light no honest candles here. The black ones, please — the dark prefers its own.
Pray if you like. The shadow grants nothing, but it never lies to you either. Rare, these days.

npcs.name: Alchemist Sythe
dialogue: Poison is just medicine with conviction. Sit further away, dear.
I need moon-herbs — proper ones, from Hollowmere's marsh. The local weeds are all dead, and dead weeds make dull poison.
Touch nothing green. Touch nothing that ISN'T green either, come to think of it.

npcs.name: Raven-Keeper Corvane
dialogue: Mind the birds. They remember faces. They remember grudges far longer.
Six ravens I keep, and six I count each dusk. Last night I counted five. The sixth is sulking, or stolen.
They fly the whole citadel, my birds. Drop me a token from each corner and I'll know my domain is whole.

npcs.name: Warden Gholl
dialogue: One prisoner. Four hundred years. We have, I think, grown fond of each other.
The lower vault stays sealed. Warlock's orders — Vesska's, not the master's. There is a difference, and it troubles me.
If you've business in the deep cells, bring me leave from one who outranks dust. I'll know it when I see it.

npcs.name: Sera the Defector
dialogue: You're warm. You're BREATHING. Oh, I could weep — do you know how long since I've seen breath?
I served the master once. Then I read what the ritual actually does, and I asked to leave. You can guess how that went.
Get me out and I'll tell you what sleeps under this citadel. It is the only currency I have left.

npcs.name: Isolde
dialogue: Dust to sweep, dust to dust. The work is eternal. So, conveniently, am I.
I dropped the master's old keys somewhere on my rounds. Four centuries of rounds. They could be anywhere.
Mind the crypt door. It sticks. Everything down here sticks, including time.

sweep: Dust to sweep, dust to dust. Four centuries in and the work still isn't done.
sleep: ...zzz... the work is eternal... so am I... zzz...

npcs.sleepDialogue: ...zzz... the work is eternal... so am I... zzz...

npcs.name: Ashka the Grimoire-Peddler
dialogue: Every hex has a price, and every price has a hex attached. Fair trade, I call it.
The towers hoard their secrets. I sell mine — cheaper, and with fewer curses attached. Usually.
One spell, properly cast, is worth a hundred swords poorly swung.

reactions.text: A dead tree, twisted and bare — something might be tucked among its roots.
A withered bush by the outer ward, worth a closer look.
A dead bush near the citadel wall, roots half-exposed.
A scrap of blackened parchment lies half-buried beside the flagstones, easy to miss.

collectible.name: Scorched Parchment
collectible.desc: A page charred at the edges, dropped somewhere near the towers.
collectible.lore: '...the wards over the east stair fail at the turn of midnight, same as always. Nobody checks then. Told no one but you, and I intend to keep it that way. — a fellow guest of the citadel'

reactions.text: A shard of black stone, half-buried near the shrine wall, bears a carving that wasn't there before.

collectible.name: Carved Shard
collectible.desc: A fragment of dark stone, etched with a symbol you don't recognize.
collectible.lore: The shadow does not explain itself, but the mark matches an old warding sign — meant to keep something IN, not out.

reactions.message: You found a strange carved shard!

reactions.text: Tucked beneath a loose flagstone near the gate approach, a torn ledger page waits to be found.

collectible.name: Torn Ledger Page
collectible.desc: A page torn from some old accounting of the citadel's stores.
collectible.lore: '...moved the last of the grave-goods behind the shrine's east wall before the warden's count. He'll never think to look there. — unsigned'

reactions.message: You found a torn ledger page! Something nearby might have shifted.

reactions.text: The stones behind the shrine wall have shifted, revealing a cache someone left behind.

collectible.name: Grave-Goods Bundle
collectible.desc: A small bundle of grave-goods, hidden away and forgotten.
collectible.lore: Whoever hid this meant to come back before the warden's count. The warden counted anyway.

reactions.message: You found a hidden cache! +25 crystals.

animals.name: Citadel Raven
dialogue: *kraa!*
The raven watches you with one glassy eye.
